description: Shared parity cases for partial budget. Expected values are hand-computed. Do not regenerate from either implementation.
proves: backend/app/services/enterprise_service.py::partial_budget and frontend/src/features/dss/partialBudget.ts::partialBudgetLocal return the same net change for the same inputs. The offline path is a second implementation of the online one; this file is the only thing that executes both and compares.
sign_convention: All four inputs are non-negative. The sign lives in which slot a quantity occupies, not in the number. net_change_ngn is returned SIGNED and UNCLAMPED: a negative result means the change is not worth making, and is a real and reportable answer.

cases.description: The sign case, and the reason this fixture exists. Verified by hand during Phase 6 by stopping agrip-backend-1 mid-session; the offline path returned -NGN 21,500.00. A sign flip between implementations must fail here, so the sign is asserted explicitly and separately from the magnitude.
The ordinary positive case. Already exercised on the backend at test_enterprise_service.py:348; now exercised on both sides with one input.

Exact zero from non-zero terms: the boundary between better off and worse off. The result must be 0 and not -0, because a negative zero rendering as "-NGN 0.00" would tell a farmer they are worse off when they are exactly even.
All zeros. Distinguishes "no change recorded" from a computation that happens to return zero. Both implementations must return 0, and neither may return null or throw.
Gains only, no losses. Exercises the loss side summing to zero without short-circuiting.
Losses only, no gains: the mirror of PB-5. Already exercised on the frontend; now on both.

Kobo precision. Catches divergence in float handling and any premature rounding. Compared at rel=1e-9, tighter than the rel=1e-4 used elsewhere in the suite. If either implementation rounds internally, this fails and that is the finding.

Cross-pair transposition trap. Swapping reduced_cost_ngn with added_cost_ngn gives 60000 - 5000 = +55000, a different figure of the opposite sign. Any implementation that confuses a saved cost for an incurred one fails here rather than passing by symmetry.
